text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zimbabwe press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Zimbabwe's ruling ZANU-PF party, which gets an annual subsidy of Z$32 million from state coffers, is bidding for at least Z$114 million from treasury in a government budget due to be unveiled in July. Part of the money will be used to set up a fund for a proposed retirement package for party executives, senior party officials told the Zimbabwe Independent.

- Chilling acts of brutality, with mothers forced to eat the flesh of their children, the wanton murder of over 3,000 people and state-induced hunger of 400,000 civilians are some of the revelations contained in a report by the Catholic Commission for Justice and Peace on a terror campaign carried out by Zimbabwe's notorious Fifth Brigade during a fight against banditry the early 1980s. The report was published in South Africa last weekend.

- State-controlled Zimbabwe Mining Development Corporation's perennial financial problems are far over over despite a recent government injection of Z$230 million to boost viability at its Mhangura Copper Mines Ltd and at Lomagundi Smelting and Mining Company, state and corporation sources told the Herald.
- Zimbabwe parliament on Thursday established a parliamentary reform committee that will enable civil society to contribute to proposed legislation and policies before they are implemented.
